ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, UBOs, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners against: (1) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (2) the Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Act); (3) the OFAC SDN List (for USD rails and transactions involving US nexus); (4) the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list; (5) the EU consolidated sanctions list; (6) the consolidated list maintained by FinCEN or equivalent foreign AML authorities where commercially reasonable; and (7) local public registers of politically exposed persons (PEPs), including federal and provincial Crown servants, judges, elected officials, and immediate family members, as defined in the PCMLTFA. Enhanced due diligence measures are mandatory for foreign PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions identified by FINTRAC/Financial Action Task Force. Ongoing transaction monitoring and re-screening every 90 days or upon any change of UBO, director, or corporate control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry, via authorized service providers (e.g., NUANS Corporation Name Search System; official registry portal accessible through corporate-registry.alberta.ca and the Alberta Corporate Registry's online NUANS search)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must include a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.' or equivalent, or the French 'Incorporée'/'Limitée'); names may be in English, French, or another language, but must be provided in an alphabet acceptable to the registry; the NUANS report must show the name in a romanized/transliterated format where the proposed name includes non-Latin script; the name must not be identical to or confusingly similar to any existing registered corporate or business name in Alberta; names of corporations incorporated federally must also be distinguishable from existing federal names, and a Canadian cross-jurisdictional search (NUANS) covering all Canadian jurisdictions is required; surnames alone, obscene or scandalous words, and names implying connection with a government entity are generally prohibited unless ministerial consent is obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Alberta Corporate Registry or the Nuans name reservation is rejected or if a search report indicates a conflict, the applicant may file a new corporate name request for a revised name; the applicant may appeal an administrative rejection by submitting a formal written request for reconsideration to the Director of Partnerships and Business Corporations under section 6 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act, providing a corrected NUANS search report, statutory declaration explaining the distinguishing elements, and any consent or waiver from the conflicting name holder; if the refusal is based on a perceived confusion with an existing name, the applicant may obtain a written consent from the prior party or may apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for a judicial review of the administrative decision; no extension of the initial 90-day reservation is granted, but a new reservation may be filed immediately; the appeal must be filed within 30 days of the rejection notice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only if the virtual office provider maintains a physical street address in Alberta, staffed during regular business hours, and is capable of receiving service of process, statutory mail, and government notices; Alberta law requires a registered office within Alberta at a specified address (no post-office box alone); the registry does not require that the registered office be the principal place of business, but the registered office must be a physical address where documents may be served during business hours; a virtual office in a commercial office building generally satisfies the statutory mandate for administrative purposes, provided that the MFO maintains actual management and operational substance in Alberta and does not use the virtual address for deceptive purposes; certain licensing requirements under Alberta Securities Commission and IIROC/FINTRAC may require additional physical presence; unannounced on-site inspection risk is elevated for this industry and is quantified as moderate-to-high.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated annual likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection for a newly incorporated Multi-Family Office holding a discretionary portfolio advisory license is approximately 35%–55% during the first 36 months of operation, rising to 60% or higher where (i) the entity acts as a principal to a trust arrangement, (ii) the entity holds securities or client assets in custody, (iii) the entity is NOT registered under the Securities Act (Alberta) or exempt market dealer regime, or (iv) any UBO or officer appears on a PEP or sanctions-related screening list; Alberta Corporate Registry, FINTRAC, Alberta Securities Commission, and municipal business licensing authorities each maintain a distinct inspection mandate; failure to maintain a physical registered office and corporate records in Alberta increases the inspection likelihood to near-certainty if a compliance complaint is filed.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, including sections 6-8 on incorporation and articles, sections 19-21 on registered and records offices, sections 102-109 on directors, sections 117-121 on officers, and sections 135-140 on corporate records and registers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation, together with the Notice of Address, Notice of Directors, and Notice of Agent for Service filed through an authorized Alberta registry agent or the Alberta Corporate Registry electronic system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for consideration authorized by the directors, subject to the Alberta Business Corporations Act. No statutory escrow account is required; subscription consideration should be received into the corporation's bank account and properly recorded in the share register and accounting records. The stated filing fee is CAD 275, converted indicatively to USD 201; exchange rates and registry fees may change.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation accept the subscription of the incorporator or subscriber for the shares specified in the subscription agreement, for the stated consideration, and issue those shares as fully paid and non-assessable, subject to receipt of consideration. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office and records office at the Alberta addresses presented to the meeting are adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until replaced or removed in accordance with law. The officers are authorized to complete registry filings, banking arrangements, books, registers, and all ancillary incorporation actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Name and Incorporation Structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized Alberta registry agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a numbered corporation or obtain an Alberta NUANS name reservation for a proposed distinctive name. Confirm that the name is not confusing with an existing corporate name or trademark. Determine whether the corporation will be incorporated under Alberta law or federally and extra-provincially registered in Alberta; this dossier assumes Alberta incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-company instruction
Alberta NUANS name reservation report, if a named corporation is selected
Ultimate beneficial ownership and control information
Registered office and records office addresses in Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended name, obtain a new reservation, or proceed with a numbered corporation. If the registry agent identifies an identity or address deficiency, provide corrected information before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Alberta registry agent and Alberta Corporate Registry electronic filing channel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation, share provisions, restrictions on share transfers, registered-office notice, records-office notice, director notice, agent-for-service notice, and incorporator information. Obtain signatures or electronic authorizations required by the filing channel. Notarization is generally not required for routine Alberta electronic incorporation, but foreign execution documents, powers of attorney, or certified identity documents should be notarized and, where applicable, legalized or apostilled.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For a rejected filing, obtain the registry rejection reason, correct the specified article or notice, and resubmit through the same registry channel. Preserve the original filing reference and evidence of payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via an authorized Alberta registry agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation package, pay the prescribed CAD 275 incorporation fee plus any name-reservation or registry-agent charges, and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, articles, corporate access number, and filed notices. Verify the legal name, incorporation date, registered addresses, directors, agent for service, and share provisions immediately upon issuance.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and filed articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, request a registry correction or file articles of amendment where required. If the filing is refused, cure the stated deficiency and resubmit; retain all registry correspondence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Initial Corporate Governance and Share Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors, with filings through Alberta Corporate Registry where a change filing is required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or obtain unanimous written resolutions. Adopt the registered and records offices, appoint officers, approve the share subscription, issue shares against received consideration, establish the securities register, approve banking authorities, adopt signing authorities, and authorize tax, accounting, privacy, and regulatory registrations. Maintain minute books and beneficial ownership records at the records office.
required_dossiers: Securities register and share certificate or uncertificated share record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a governance defect is identified, ratify the action by a valid board or shareholder resolution, correct the securities register, and make any required Alberta Corporate Registry update. Obtain legal advice before retroactive documentation of material transactions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Operating Business and Securities Activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Canada Revenue Agency, and Alberta Securities Commission through the National Registration Database, as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the CRA business number and applicable GST/HST, payroll, and corporate income-tax accounts. Analyze whether the multi-family office provides portfolio management, investment fund management, dealing, advising, custody, or referral services. If registration is required, file the applicable Form 33-109 and firm registration applications through NRD before commencing regulated activity. Do not hold client assets or transmit client funds unless the relevant regulatory and custodial arrangements are approved.
required_dossiers: GST/HST and payroll registration information, if applicable
Proficiency, insurance, financial-condition, and audited-financial information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to Alberta Securities Commission deficiency letters within the specified period, amend the NRD application, and provide supplemental policies or financial information. If registration is denied or restricted, suspend the affected activity and pursue reconsideration, amendment, or an available exemption only after written legal analysis.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Securities Commission for portfolio-advisory and investment-management registration; the applicable municipality for development, business-licence, occupancy, and fire-safety approvals. This is an office-based financial-services business rather than a manufacturing facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Portfolio Manager and, where applicable, Investment Fund Manager registration under the Alberta Securities Act, National Instrument 31-103 Registration Requirements, Exemptions and Ongoing Registrant Obligations, and related Canadian securities instruments. A municipal business licence or occupancy approval may also be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from a project-level environmental impact assessment for ordinary leased office premises with no industrial construction, process plant, regulated emissions, or material waste stream. A project-specific review may arise if premises construction, redevelopment, or regulated activities are added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine industrial wastewater, process VOC, or stack-emission authorization is ordinarily applicable to a standard office. The corporation must comply with the Alberta Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, applicable waste legislation, municipal sewer bylaws, hazardous-material rules, and any site-specific approval. Office waste, electronic waste, batteries, confidential records, and cleaning chemicals must be segregated and transferred through lawful disposal or recycling channels. Any regulated discharge or emission requires prior permit review and compliance with permit-specific limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal development, occupancy, and business approvals where required; confirm building-code compliance, occupant load, accessibility, emergency egress, fire-alarm and sprinkler certification, and workplace health and safety arrangements. Coordinate fire inspection or occupancy clearance with the relevant municipal fire authority. Structural load inspection is required where the premises are altered, equipment is installed, or the authority having jurisdiction requires it. Comply with Alberta Occupational Health and Safety legislation, including emergency procedures, incident reporting, violence prevention, first aid, and safe-work requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Number (BN) registration and GST/HST portal via My Business Account; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance (ATBF) for provincial Corporate Income Tax, administered and collected by CRA under a federal-provincial tax collection agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must file Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) with CRA or apply online through CRA 'My Business Account' to obtain a 9-digit BN and associated GST/HST, corporate income tax, and payroll program accounts. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada must register for a BN; no separate Alberta provincial registration is required as Alberta's corporate income tax is collected by CRA. Supporting documentation includes the certificate of incorporation, registered office address, and proof of Canadian resident director or applicable provincial licence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Canadian law; corporations are taxed at the entity level under the Income Tax Act. Available elections include: (i) Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) status for the small business deduction; (ii) GST/HST group registration under s.156 ETA; (iii) hybrid mismatch adjustments under ss.18.2/18.3 ITA; (iv) functional currency election under s.261 ITA.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST); Alberta applies the 5% federal GST only, with no provincial sales tax or HST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies for the current calendar quarter and the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; non-resident suppliers of digital or remote services are also required to register if they exceed the same CAD 30,000 threshold of Canadian-source supplies in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory e-invoicing, or digital stamping regime is in effect. Registered suppliers must issue tax invoices containing prescribed disclosures (supplier name and GST/HST number, transaction date, taxable supply description, consideration, and tax payable); electronic invoices are permitted. CRA may require electronic access to books and records. Platform operators may be deemed to make underlying supplies in the marketplace context.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of goods exported or services rendered to non-residents who are not in Canada, but financial services are generally exempt unless supplied to non-residents and not related to the administration of a Canadian investment plan. MFO services (fee-based portfolio advisory and discretionary investment management) may qualify as zero-rated exports if the recipient is a non-resident throughout the supply, no goods or real property in Canada are involved, and the service is not characterized as an exempt 'financial service' under ETA Schedule VI Part IX.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canada Customs Export Declaration (G7 / Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED))
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing export from Canada
Evidence of non-resident status of recipient (e.g., overseas address, passport/ID, certificate of residence)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire payment record from the non-resident client
Executed service agreement and detailed service scope
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess GST/HST for up to four years (or indefinitely in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or neglect), deny zero-rating on the basis of insufficient or contemporaneous documentation, charge arrears interest, and impose penalties of up to 25% of the tax amount under s.285.1 ETA, plus an additional 50% of the benefit for gross negligence; criminal prosecution under s.327 ETA carries fines up to CAD 100,000 and/or imprisonment. Retroactive clawbacks are standard when export documentation is incomplete or inconsistent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. Canada has no general foreign-exchange administration imposing exchange controls. The Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions supervises federally regulated financial institutions; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada administers applicable anti-money-laundering and terrorist-financing reporting requirements. Alberta securities regulation is administered by the Alberta Securities Commission.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible, and Canada generally imposes no controls on capital-account transfers, foreign investment, dividends, interest, or repatriation of investment proceeds. Transfers remain subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, tax law, corporate-law restrictions, contractual covenants, and bank due diligence. An Alberta corporation may remit dividends only when authorized under the applicable corporate statute and when statutory solvency tests are met. Payments to non-residents may trigger Canadian withholding tax, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. A multi-family office providing discretionary portfolio advice may require registration under provincial securities laws; custody, dealing, investment-fund, or portfolio-management activities can create additional registration and compliance obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no general statutory requirement to repatriate export proceeds or convert a prescribed portion of foreign-currency receipts into Canadian dollars. Export receipts may be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted commercially. Exporters must comply with applicable customs, sanctions, tax, contractual, and bank documentation requirements; banks may request invoices, shipping evidence, client instructions, and the payment purpose.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium for an offshore electronic-money institution as the primary Canadian banking or client-funds solution. Canada does not generally recognize a foreign EMI account as a substitute for a Canadian deposit-taking institution or for legally compliant custody or client-money arrangements. Use may be possible for the corporation's own operating funds, subject to the provider's geographic eligibility, Canadian payment access, sanctions screening, source-of-funds checks, and contractual terms. Do not route client assets through an operating account or payment intermediary unless the arrangement is expressly permitted by securities, trust, custody, and payment-services requirements. Verify the provider's Canadian regulatory status and any applicable Retail Payment Activities Act registration obligations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian law does not impose a universal in-person director interview or physical account-opening requirement. Banks set their own onboarding standards and may require an in-person or live-video interview, certified identity documents, Canadian address evidence, or a Canadian signing officer. Non-resident directors and beneficial owners may be onboarded remotely at a bank's discretion; remote acceptance is not guaranteed. Expect enhanced review for a high-risk, cross-border multi-family office and confirm requirements with the selected bank before incorporation or funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discretionary investment advice, portfolio management, dealing, custody, or client-money activity without a clearly established provincial securities registration or exemption position.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Securities Commission registration analysis; registration certificates or documented exemption basis; service descriptions and client agreements; organizational and supervisory charts; custody and client-asset flow diagrams; compliance policies; and evidence that banking accounts are not being used to commingle client assets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership, family relationships, control, or use of nominee entities, trusts, private holding companies, or offshore structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registry records; articles and bylaws; shareholder and control registers; organization chart to natural-person ultimate beneficial owners; trust deeds and trustee, settlor, protector, and beneficiary details where relevant; director and authorized-signatory resolutions; and certified identity and residential-address evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or irregular inbound capital, third-party funding, transfers through multiple jurisdictions, or funds inconsistent with the corporation's stated advisory business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital subscription and shareholder-loan agreements; board approvals; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; audited or tax-return financial statements where available; originating-account statements; remitter and beneficiary details; transaction purpose and expected-volume profile; and a reconciliation linking each transfer to its legal and accounting basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments for clients, beneficiaries, or related parties, including pooled flows, custody-like activity, or unexplained pass-through transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written funds-flow map; client mandates and agreements; account ownership and custody documentation; transaction-level supporting records; segregation and reconciliation controls; explanation of the corporation's role; and legal advice confirming the proposed activity is consistent with applicable securities, trust, and payment-services requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed persons, adverse media, high-risk jurisdictions, or unexplained counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented risk-based screening results; identity and beneficial-owner verification; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds records; counterparty and jurisdiction rationale; escalation and approval records; and enhanced monitoring procedures. Screening and reporting obligations must be assessed under applicable Canadian law and bank policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unsubstantiated business substance, inconsistent stated revenue, or inability to explain the economic purpose of cross-border transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan; Alberta registered-office and operating-address evidence; service-provider and staffing records; client and mandate documentation with appropriate confidentiality protections; projected transaction volumes and geographies; invoices; tax registrations and filings; and a written treasury and payment-control policy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Receive capital contributions and shareholder loans into a corporate account held in the corporation's legal name at a Canadian financial institution. Use the originating bank's SWIFT transfer instructions, accurate beneficiary and intermediary-bank details, and a payment narrative identifying the legal purpose, such as share subscription or shareholder loan; Canada has no generally prescribed foreign-exchange purpose-code system for these transfers. Retain subscription or loan agreements, board resolutions, ownership records, source-of-funds evidence, and remitter details. Reconcile receipts to the general ledger and promptly answer bank requests. Do not accept unexplained third-party deposits or route investor funds through personal, client, or unrelated accounts. Assess withholding tax, transfer-pricing, thin-capitalization, and other tax consequences for cross-border related-party financing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the corporation's own legitimate operating and professional-service payments, use bank wire transfers, commonly SWIFT MT103, with verified beneficiary details, a clear payment purpose, invoices or contracts, and supporting approval records. For eligible cross-border goods transactions, a commercial documentary letter of credit may be available subject to bank underwriting, documentary terms, and applicable trade rules. An MFO's advisory business is principally service-based; securities trades, custody transfers, and client payments should use appropriately authorized custodians or brokers and documented client mandates, not be mischaracterized as trade disbursements. Banks may request contracts, invoices, tax information, sanctions screening, and evidence of the transaction's commercial purpose.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards used to manage documented corporate operating, investment, or financing exposures, subject to bank credit approval and suitability controls.
Non-deliverable forwards where commercially appropriate and accepted by the counterparty; settlement, reporting, and documentation requirements depend on the product and parties.
Currency swaps used for documented funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to counterparty approval and applicable derivatives documentation, reporting, and conduct requirements.
Spot foreign-exchange transactions for operational conversion needs.

Options or other derivatives only where permitted by the corporation's governing authority, applicable securities and derivatives rules, counterparty terms, and documented risk-management mandate; speculative activity should not be assumed permissible.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File annually within two months after the corporation's anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in notices, administrative dissolution, loss of corporate status, and restoration costs. The official fee is CAD 20, converted approximately to USD.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canada Business Corporations Act Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a federal corporation, file annually within 60 days after the anniversary date; online filing fee is CAD 12.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two or more consecutive years may lead to administrative dissolution after notice. Restoration and filing fees apply. The official fee is CAD 12, converted approximately to USD.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Required annually for a federal corporation registered to carry on business in Alberta; deadline follows the Alberta extra-provincial registration anniversary rule.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the extra-provincial registration may result in cancellation of the registration, inability to rely on the registration for Alberta operations, and reinstatement or re-registration requirements. Fee converted approximately from CAD.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register of Individuals with Significant Control Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, where the corporation is federally incorporated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File beneficial ownership information with the federal annual return within 60 days after the anniversary date and update changes within 15 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance may constitute an offence and may expose the corporation and responsible directors or officers to statutory penalties. Alberta corporations generally maintain ownership information internally unless another filing regime applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general revenue or asset threshold automatically requires an audit for a typical private Alberta or federal corporation. An auditor is generally required unless the applicable corporate statute permits and shareholders validly approve an audit exemption. Publicly accountable, reporting-issuer, regulated financial, or licensed investment businesses may require an audit under corporate, securities, or sector-specific rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP under Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for eligible private corporations; IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises or where required by securities, financing, regulatory, or contractual requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain current ownership and control information in the corporate records. A federal corporation must maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control, confirm or update the information with its federal annual return, and record changes within 15 days. Alberta corporations must update internal registers and provide ownership information when legally required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control, where the Canada Business Corporations Act applies
Articles, bylaws, resolutions, and issued share records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 300-1,200 annually, excluding exceptional filings, nominee services, and tax or regulatory work
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,000-25,000 for a typical private corporation; regulated financial or investment businesses may incur substantially higher fees

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined federal and Alberta general corporate income tax rate (federal 15%: 38% statutory base minus 10% provincial abatement minus 13% General Rate Reduction; Alberta 8%); 11% combined rate on the first CAD $500,000 of qualifying active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (federal 9% + Alberta 2%); passive investment income of the MFO holding corporation bears an integrated federal rate of 38⅔% on aggregate investment income (30⅔% refundable as Refundable Dividend Tax On Hand) plus Alberta 8%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction is unavailable to a specified investment business unless the MFO employs more than five full-time employees; RDTOH integration mechanics for portfolio dividends and investment income; Section 126 foreign tax credits; investment tax credits for qualified Canadian resource and clean-energy expenditures; no Alberta capital tax for investment-holding entities other than regulated financial institutions.
